findings.evidence: DOM order is #s3-step3 (style="order:3", text "Confirm your order"), then #s3-step2 (style="order:2", text "Enter payment details"), then #s3-step1 (style="order:1", text "Choose a plan")
findings.fix: Reorder the markup itself so DOM order already reads Choose a plan, Enter payment details, Confirm your order, and drop the CSS order property, or otherwise make the linearized reading match the visual sequence.
findings.violation: The CSS order property reverses the visual sequence of the steps relative to their DOM order, so a reader encountering the content linearized (CSS removed, or read by a screen reader) hears the confirmation step before the plan-choosing and payment steps it depends on, reversing the actual decision sequence.

findings.evidence: The entire page exposes only two links inside <nav id="nav"> ("Plan a trip", "Service alerts"); there is no search form, no sitemap link, and no breadcrumb trail anywhere in the document
findings.fix: Add a second independent way to reach this page or its content, such as a site search form or a link into a site map, rather than relying solely on the primary navigation menu.
findings.violation: The page offers only one mechanism (the primary navigation menu) for locating this content, and the page is a general informational update, not one step in a linear process exempt from the requirement for a second mechanism.

findings.evidence: , with no role, tabindex, or aria-label attribute anywhere on the div or its child image
findings.fix: Replace the div with a native button element, or add role="button", tabindex="0", a keyboard handler, and an accessible name such as aria-label="Delete" that states what activating the control does.
findings.violation: A custom interactive control built from a generic div carries no role, no programmatically determinable accessible name (the only content is an image with alt="", marked decorative), and no keyboard access point, so a screen reader does not expose it as a control at all.

findings.evidence: <label for="phone" id="s3-form-phone-label" style="color:#cc0000">Phone number</label>, the only one of the form's four labels styled in red, with no asterisk, "required" text, icon, or other non-color signal attached
findings.fix: Add a visible, non-color signal alongside the color, such as a "required" word or an asterisk with an accessible description, so the distinction survives for a reader who cannot perceive color.
findings.violation: Color alone distinguishes this label from the form's other labels, with no accompanying text, icon, or other non-color signal carrying whatever meaning the color is meant to convey.

findings.evidence: The heading reads "Accessibility improvements", but the section's own paragraphs (#s1-p1, #s1-p2) describe requesting a fare adjustment and checking real-time arrivals by phone; the only accessibility-related content is one image's alt text about repainting accessible parking spaces.
findings.fix: Retitle the heading to name what the section is actually about, for example "Fares and real-time updates", or move the fare-adjustment and arrivals paragraphs under a heading that already covers them.
findings.violation: The heading's wording does not describe the topic of the content that actually follows it, so a reader scanning headings cannot predict this section covers fare adjustments and real-time arrival information.

findings.evidence: The heading reads "Weekend service", but the section's content (#s2-p1, a fare-adjustment paragraph duplicated from section 1, and the #s2-table1 zone status table) never mentions weekends or weekend scheduling at all.
findings.fix: Retitle the heading to match the actual content, for example "Zone status", or add the weekend-specific content the heading promises.
findings.violation: The heading's wording misdescribes the content that follows it: nothing in the section concerns weekend service specifically.

findings.evidence: Error., with no aria-describedby on #promo linking it to this span
findings.fix: Replace "Error." with text that names the field and the actual problem, for example "Promo code not recognized", and link it to the input with aria-describedby.
findings.violation: The error text associated with the invalid promo field is fully generic ("Error."), naming neither the field nor the specific problem, and it is not programmatically linked to the field it describes.
